picks.t: SC: citizens can prosecute false affidavits
picks.what: The Supreme Court (Justices Datta and Nagu, judgment reported 19 October) held that any private individual, not only a public servant, can file a criminal complaint under Section 125A of the RP Act, 1951 against a candidate who gives false information or conceals facts in nomination papers.
picks.prelims: Section 33A of the RP Act, 1951 requires candidates to disclose pending cases and convictions. Section 125A makes false information or concealment in the nomination affidavit punishable with up to six months' imprisonment, a fine, or both.
picks.mains: Use in GS2 answers on electoral reforms and criminalisation of politics: disclosure works only when it is enforced, and the ruling lets every voter enforce it. Mention the risk of vexatious complaints for balance.

picks.what: Congress announced, on behalf of the INDIA bloc, a 'public impeachment proceeding' against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on 30 October over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, reopening the question of how a CEC can be removed.
picks.prelims: Under Article 324(5), the CEC can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds of a Supreme Court judge (Article 124(4)). Other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the CEC's recommendation.
picks.mains: Use in GS2 answers on the independence of constitutional bodies: security of tenure shields the CEC, while the appointment process under the CEC Act, 2023 remains debated.

picks.what: UNEP's 17th Emissions Gap Report, 'The Point of Return' (21 October), says limiting warming to 1.5°C without significant overshoot is no longer possible. Full implementation of current pledges points to about 2.6°C.
picks.prelims: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to hold warming well below 2°C and to pursue 1.5°C; countries pledge cuts through NDCs. UNEP's annual Emissions Gap Report measures the gap between pledges and those goals.
picks.mains: Use in GS3 answers on climate negotiations and India's commitments: India's low per-capita emissions support its equity and CBDR-RC arguments.

picks.t: CBD COP17 runs first global KMGBF review
picks.what: COP17 to the Convention on Biological Diversity in Yerevan, Armenia (19–30 October) is holding the first global review of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Parties themselves rate fewer than half of their national targets as on track.
picks.prelims: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted at CBD COP15 in Montreal in December 2022. It has 23 targets for 2030, including '30x30': conserving 30% of land and 30% of sea.
picks.mains: Use in GS3 answers on biodiversity governance, conservation finance and benefit-sharing; India's updated NBSAP and the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023 show domestic alignment.

picks.t: SC: bail when pre-trial detention drags
picks.what: In mid-October the Supreme Court (Justices Datta and Nagu) granted bail to former Rajasthan minister Mahesh Joshi in the ACB's Jal Jeevan Mission tender case, holding that prolonged pre-trial detention cannot become punishment without trial.
picks.prelims: Section 479 of the BNSS: an undertrial who has served half the maximum sentence for the offence must be released on bail, and a first-time offender after one-third. It does not apply to offences punishable with death or life imprisonment.
picks.mains: Use in GS2 answers on criminal-justice reform and judicial delays: with nearly three in four prisoners undertrials, bail delay is a structural injustice under Article 21, not an individual one.

picks.t: India–New Zealand FTA comes into force
picks.what: The India–New Zealand FTA, signed on 27 April, took effect on 20 October, giving all Indian exports duty-free access to New Zealand.
picks.prelims: India left the RCEP talks in 2019 and has since signed deals with developed economies: the ECTA with Australia (2022), the TEPA with EFTA (2024) and the CETA with the UK (2025).
picks.mains: Use in GS2 and GS3 answers on India's trade strategy after RCEP and on export-led manufacturing.

picks.t: Cyclone watch on the Andhra coast
picks.what: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam around the forenoon of 28 October as a very severe cyclonic storm. Odisha cancelled officials' leave and deployed NDRF and ODRAF teams.
picks.prelims: The north Indian Ocean has two cyclone seasons: April–June and October–December. The Bay of Bengal sees far more cyclones than the Arabian Sea, and IMD New Delhi is the regional centre that names them.
picks.mains: Use in GS1 answers on tropical cyclones and in GS3 disaster-management answers on early warning and evacuation.

picks.t: Ladakh: hill councils recast, new districts
picks.what: The President promulgated the LAHDC (Amendment) Regulation, 2026, paving the way for hill councils in all eight of Ladakh's districts, as an MHA draft proposes a UT-wide elected body. Ladakh's groups still seek Statehood or Sixth Schedule protection.
picks.prelims: Ladakh is a Union Territory without a legislature, so the President can make regulations for it under Article 240. The Sixth Schedule, by contrast, sets up autonomous district councils in tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
picks.mains: Use in GS2 answers on UT governance, decentralisation and tribal autonomy: statutory hill councils versus constitutional Sixth Schedule protection.

picks.t: Ethanol tender shifts feedstock to grain
picks.what: Oil marketing companies' ethanol tender for 2026-27 excludes ethanol from sugarcane juice, sugar, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses after the Centre set sugar diversion for ethanol to zero, leaving C-heavy molasses and grains (maize, FCI rice, damaged grains) to supply it.
picks.prelims: The National Policy on Biofuels, 2018 (amended 2022) allows ethanol from sugarcane juice, molasses, damaged food grains and surplus grains, and brought the 20% blending (E20) target forward to 2025-26.
picks.mains: Use in GS3 answers on energy security and the food–fuel trade-off: feedstock choices tie fuel policy to maize and sugar markets.

picks.t: DPDP breach-report rule not in force yet
picks.what: A CBFC film-certification portal leak and an SBI disclosure of 3,897 customer records on the dark web came to light within days, while the DPDP Act's breach-notification duty takes legal effect only on 13 May 2027.
picks.prelims: Section 8(6) of the DPDP Act, 2023 requires a data fiduciary to report a personal-data breach to the Data Protection Board and to each affected person. Separately, CERT-In's 2022 directions require cyber incidents to be reported within 6 hours.
picks.mains: Use in GS3 answers on cyber security and GS2 answers on privacy (Puttaswamy, 2017): a right needs an enforceable breach duty, not just a law on paper.

facts: The CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge; other Election Commissioners only on the CEC's recommendation.
RP Act S.125A: false information in a nomination affidavit can mean up to 6 months' jail, a fine, or both.
The Kunming-Montreal framework (CBD COP15, 2022) has 23 targets for 2030, including '30x30'.
BNSS S.479: an undertrial who has served half the maximum sentence must get bail; a first-time offender after one-third.
UNEP's Emissions Gap Report compares countries' pledges with the cuts needed for the Paris goals.

mcqs.s: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed by the President on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers.
mcqs.why: Only like an SC judge: an address by each House by special majority (Art 324(5), 124(4)).

mcqs.s: Under India's National Policy on Biofuels, damaged food grains unfit for human consumption can be used to make ethanol.
mcqs.why: The 2018 policy widened feedstocks to include them.

mainsQ.q: Mandatory disclosure of candidates' criminal records, assets and liabilities was meant to enable informed voting. Examine how far the law enforces truthful disclosure, and suggest how voters can become an effective check.
mainsQ.hint: Use: S.33A and S.125A of the RP Act, ADR (2002) and PUCL (2003), the October 2026 ruling allowing private complaints under S.125A, and the risk of vexatious cases.
